drafts.title: Charge port clearly shows charging state at a glance
drafts.description: When plugged in, the charge-port indicator communicates charging, fully charged and fault states in a way any user can understand without opening the door or the app.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: From a standing position 1.5 m (5 ft) away in daylight, an observer must be able to distinguish charging / complete / error state within 2 seconds in 9 out of 10 trials using the charge-port indicator alone.
assumptions: Indicator will use visually distinct colors or flash patterns that are legible in daylight.
Basic user vision limitations (e.g. common forms of color weakness) will be considered in indicator design.
uncertainties: Very bright direct sunlight or extreme dirt on the charge port could reduce legibility.
Local regulations may constrain allowed indicator colors or brightness.

drafts.title: Navigation/trip planner presents only chargers compatible for this vehicle and shows connector/availability clearly
drafts.description: When planning a trip or searching for a fast-charge stop, the vehicle lists chargers that are compatible with this car (connector and supported charging mode) and shows connector type and expected availability so drivers can choose a correct stop without trial-and-error.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a 200-mile simulated route with three planned charging stops, the system must (a) present only chargers compatible with the vehicle's charging interfaces for at least 95% of recommended stops, and (b) allow a driver to identify connector type and available stalls for a suggested charger within 5 seconds in 9 of 10 trials.
assumptions: Third-party charger network data must include connector/type and availability information.
Vehicle has network connectivity during route planning or uses recently cached charger metadata.
uncertainties: Data quality and timeliness from external providers may vary by region and operator.
Compatibility definitions must cover regional connector variants and adapters.

drafts.title: Long-range BEV variant targeted for true real-world range customers expect
drafts.description: Offer a long-range battery-electric variant engineered to deliver noticeably longer single-charge range so customers can complete long drives with fewer interruptions.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Long-range BEV variant must achieve at least 400 miles real-world range as measured by EPA combined procedure and validated by three independent real-world highway/city tests (averaged), across temperate conditions (10–25°C).
assumptions: Successor launch (3–5 years) will include higher-energy battery cells and aerodynamic/weight improvements compared to the current model.

Customers explicitly asked for 600–700 miles; achieving 600+ would likely require next-generation cell chemistries (e.g., solid-state at ~400 Wh/kg) or significant reductions in vehicle energy consumption.
uncertainties: Actual achievable range depends on final battery energy density, vehicle mass and packaging tradeoffs.
Cold-weather and high-speed conditions will reduce real-world range below the measured average; battery degradation over time may affect long-term attainment of this metric.

drafts.title: Reduce perceived harshness on broken pavement
drafts.description: Customers should not feel the ride is harsh on broken or patched pavement—bumps and irregularities should be absorbed so occupants feel comfortable on typical poor-quality roads.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a standardized rough-road circuit driven at 30–50 mph, the average perceived harshness score from a blinded panel of 10 customers must improve by at least 25% compared with the current 5 Series baseline; at least 8 of 10 panelists must rate the successor as noticeably smoother.
assumptions: Improvements will be realized by chassis tuning, damping strategies, tires and possible active systems available for the successor generation.
Baseline perceived-harshness scores are available from prior model testing for direct comparison.
uncertainties: Trade-offs between sporty handling and low-speed compliance may require configurable modes.
Very large potholes beyond the test profile might still be felt and are out of scope for this metric.

drafts.title: Reduce distracting wind noise at highway speeds above 70 mph
drafts.description: At highway speeds, wind noise should not be a distracting source of fatigue or interfere with conversations and in-car audio.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Measured interior wind-noise level at the driver's ear shall be ≤ 66 dB(A) at 75 mph on a representative highway stretch (windows closed, vents off), and subjective driver annoyance rating must be improved by at least 30% vs the current 5 Series in a blinded panel.
assumptions: Test conditions assume clean seals, standard production mirrors and roof features.
Improvements can come from aero sealing, mirror/trim design and glazing/seal enhancements.
uncertainties: Accessory roof rails, open windows, and aftermarket add-ons can increase wind noise beyond this target.
Different body configurations (sunroof/panoramic) may require variant-specific tuning to meet the target.

drafts.title: Lane-keeping assist behavior is smooth and predictable in curves
drafts.description: When lane-keeping assistance is active, steering adjustments in curves must feel gradual and predictable rather than abrupt or 'nervous', so drivers are comfortable with the system.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Across 20 standardized curved-road maneuvers between 50–75 mph, the system must not perform abrupt lane-centering corrections in more than 2 of 20 trials (abrupt defined as a steering correction that requires a driver counter-steer within 1.5 seconds in the test), and the frequency of abrupt interventions must be reduced by ≥80% versus the current model in the same test protocol.
assumptions: Standardized test protocol and driver-panel definitions for 'abrupt' interventions will be used for objective comparison.
Improvements may come from tuning control gains, previewing curvature and smoothing of steering outputs.
uncertainties: Driver perception of 'nervous' behavior varies; test panel composition can affect results.
Some rare road geometries may still trigger assertive corrections for safety reasons.

drafts.title: Level 3 type approval request (customer ask)
drafts.description: Customers request that the car obtains type approval for Level 3 automated driving in Germany.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a regulatory/type-approval request from customers; the request is recorded for legal/homologation evaluation and is out of scope for product-level customer-experience requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory / homologation request (type approval). Out of scope for product requirement drafting.

drafts.title: CARB emission limits compliance request (customer ask)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the powertrain complies with CARB emission limits in all US states.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a regulatory compliance request; handling and verification belong to homologation and legal teams and are out of scope for product-level requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory / emissions certification request. Out of scope for product requirements.

drafts.title: UN R155 cybersecurity approval request (customer ask)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the vehicle fulfils UN R155 cybersecurity type approval.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a cybersecurity type-approval request; certification decisions and evidence are handled by compliance and engineering and are out of scope for customer-facing requirement drafts.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory / certification request. Out of scope for product requirement drafting.

drafts.title: EU battery passport compliance request (customer ask)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the battery complies with the EU battery passport regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a regulatory/data-reporting request; implementing and certifying the battery passport lies with compliance and supply-chain teams and is out of scope for customer-facing requirement drafting.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory / data reporting request. Out of scope for product requirements.

drafts.title: 800 V electrical architecture request (customer ask)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the car use an 800 V electrical architecture.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is an engineering architecture request from customers; it is an implementation/engineering specification and is out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering specification (electrical architecture). Out of scope for customer-facing requirement drafting.

drafts.title: 22 kW onboard AC charger upgrade request (customer ask)
drafts.description: Customers request that the onboard AC charger be upgraded to 22 kW.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a hardware/engineering specification request (onboard charger power). It is out of scope for customer-facing requirement drafts and should be handled as an engineering spec.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering specification (onboard charger power). Out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Request for solid-state battery cells with 400 Wh/kg
drafts.description: Customers request the battery use solid-state cells achieving ~400 Wh/kg energy density.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a cell-technology performance request; it is an engineering/materials specification and out of scope for customer-facing requirements. It is recorded for product strategy and technology planning.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering/materials specification (cell chemistry and energy density). Out of scope for customer-facing requirement drafting.

drafts.title: Front brake disc diameter request (395 mm)
drafts.description: Customers request front brake discs with a diameter of 395 mm.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a component-dimension request (brake disc diameter). It is an engineering specification and out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering specification (component dimension). Out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Request to use a specific lidar supplier for highway assist
drafts.description: Customers request that highway assist uses a lidar sensor from a named supplier.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a supplier/component preference; selecting specific hardware suppliers is an engineering/procurement decision and out of scope for customer-facing requirement drafting.
drafts.scope_reason: Supplier/component preference. Out of scope for product requirement drafting.
